title: verify your model's predictions

atoms.evidence: @t.inference_mode() decorator on predict(); explicit no-gradient inference pass

model.eval() called inside predict — switches batchnorm to use running stats; the exercise comment explicitly says 'if your model is predicting roughly the same percentage for every category, the weights are randomly initialized'
logits.softmax(dim=-1).max(dim=-1) returns (max_probs, predicted_indices) — top-1 prediction (the seed atom is named topk but the exercise uses k=1 via .max which returns the same tuple shape)

notes: Inference-only exercise — 3 atoms, all from the eval/inference cluster. topk-predictions matches loosely (it's .max(dim=-1) not .topk) but the conceptual atom — converting logits to a ranked prediction — is identical. First firing of train-eval-mode-branch confirms it's real (BatchNorm running stats need eval mode to behave correctly).
